messages.content: Write an incident report for a two-hour outage of a payment API caused by a expired TLS certificate. Around 200 words.

## Incident Report — Payments API Outage

Date: 2 September 2026
Duration: 09:14–11:22 UTC (2h 08m)
Impact: All `/v1/charges` and `/v1/refunds` calls failed TLS handshake. Roughly 41,000 transactions rejected; no data loss, no unauthorized access.

### What happened

The certificate for `api.payments.internal` expired at 09:14 UTC. Client SDKs and our own gateway both refused the connection, so the failure was total rather than degraded. Renewal had been automated in 2024 through cert-manager, but this host was migrated to the new cluster in July and its Certificate resource was never recreated. Nothing was watching the old host, and the 30-day expiry alert routed to a Slack channel we archived in June.

### Recovery

An on-call engineer traced the handshake error at 10:40 after the first hour went into generic 502 triage. A replacement certificate was issued manually and rolled out at 11:18. Traffic recovered fully by 11:22.

### Follow-up

1. Audit every TLS endpoint for a matching cert-manager resource — owner: platform, due 12 Sept.
2. Move expiry alerts to PagerDuty, at 45 and 14 days.
3. Add a synthetic probe that fails loudly on handshake errors, not just HTTP status.
Add a timeline with the four key moments.

### Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:14 | Certificate for `api.payments.internal` expires. All TLS handshakes start failing. |
| 09:21 | Error-rate alarm pages on-call. Triage begins against the gateway's generic 502s. |
| 10:40 | On-call reads the raw handshake error and identifies the expired certificate. |
| 11:18 | Manually issued certificate rolled out. Traffic fully recovered by 11:22. |

### What happened

The certificate expired at 09:14 UTC. Client SDKs and our own gateway both refused the connection, so the failure was total rather than degraded. Renewal had been automated in 2024 through cert-manager, but this host was migrated to the new cluster in July and its Certificate resource was never recreated. Nothing was watching the old host, and the 30-day expiry alert routed to a Slack channel we archived in June.

The first 79 minutes went to the wrong layer. The gateway masked the handshake failure as a 502, so the on-call engineer chased upstream health before looking at the transport.

### Follow-up

1. Audit every TLS endpoint for a matching cert-manager resource — owner: platform, due 12 Sept.
2. Move expiry alerts to PagerDuty, at 45 and 14 days.
3. Add a synthetic probe that fails loudly on handshake errors, not just HTTP status.
4. Stop the gateway collapsing TLS failures into 502.
